item.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) throws the ball during the first half against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. It's going to be a wild week, but we have a lot less time to prepare for Week 12 because of the holiday schedule. That's why we have to get our rankings out so you get your lineups set for this huge fantasy football week. We have no bye weeks, so every healthy body is in play. As always, we start at the top. These are our fantasy football quarterback rankings for Week 12. Quarterback Rankings: Week 12 QB Joe Burrow, Cincinnati Bengals Over the past month or so, Burrow has begun to push Josh Allen for that top quarterback spot weekly in the rankings. In Week 12, Burrow once again steals that No. 1 spot from Allen this holiday weekend. Burrow has an average matchup against the New Orleans Saints, while Allen has to go up against a Chiefs' defense that is allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks this season. QB Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs Mahomes has been red hot and will look to keep that going in a potential shootout against the Buffalo Bills this week, in a game that could go a long way in helping determine the No. 1 seed in the AFC Playoffs. We have him two spots above ECR (expert consensus ranking) as the QB5 overall this week. We expect there to be plenty of fantasy points to go around this week in Buffalo. QB Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers Purdy is one of the most intriguing quarterbacks of the week. While he has been great this season, he has a brutal matchup this week against the Seattle Seahawks. We have him one spot below in ECR as our QB9 overall this week. However, he does have the upside to outperform his current ranking now that he is beginning to get his weapons back and healthy. QB Michael Penix Jr, Atlanta Falcons Of every projected starting quarterback this week, Penix comes in last in our rankings as the QB32. That matchup against the Minnesota Vikings is terrible and particularly difficult for an already subpar quarterback in an offense that builds off the rushing attack. It's going to be a long day for Penix and the Falcons' offense. item.title: The story that ended Trev Alberts’ Michigan AD tenure before it even began
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-USA TODAY Sports The story that ended Trev Alberts’ Michigan AD tenure before it even began appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michigan has decided not to hire Trev Alberts as the next athletic director. Michigan reversed course on the hire on Tuesday , even though there was a memorandum of understanding signed between the two sides. Now, the story that ended the Alberts’ tenure before it even began has come to light. David Covucci of FOIAball found a lawsuit that involved Trev Alberts, who was then the Nebraska AD. The lawsuit was filed in 2024 by Ashley Scoggin against the Nebraska Board of Regents, the school’s women’s basketball coach, and then-AD Alberts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “According to the lawsuit, during an away game, a student-manager duped a hotel employee into giving out a card key to assistant coach Chuck Love’s room. Two players used the card to enter Love’s room and filmed Scoggin in his bed. Presented with the video, head coach Amy Williams allegedly called a meeting and allowed the entire team to confront Scoggin over the relationship,” Covucci wrote. “Scoggin was initially suspended. Back in Nebraska, she was kicked off the team. Love was suspended with pay and allowed to quietly resign three months later. Alberts eventually agreed to pay Love $136,000 in severance. The lawsuit accuses Alberts of violating Scoggin’s civil rights after learning of the relationship by approving of her removal from the team, refusing to order an investigation, and encouraging her to leave the school.” The lawsuit led to two different depositions of Alberts, and some shocking details from the depositions came to light. First, he did not know he had been named vice chancellor at Nebraska. Meanwhile, he also gave some evasive answers about relationships between staff and students. “Faculty or Staff members are prohibited from engaging in any romantic relationship with an undergraduate student,” the Nebraska policy on consensual relationships reads. Alberts was given a copy of the policy, and then asked, “College coaches should never have sex with the student-athletes that they are coaching. True?” “I don’t know how to answer that,” Alberts replied. “I mean, you know, it just depends.” Alberts also said he tried not to pay attention to relationships. Considering the situation at Michigan with Sherrone Moore, maybe Alberts was not the right choice to begin with. item.title: Massachusetts high school football inks endorsement deal with New Balance
item.description: Massachusetts’ first five-star quarterback has signed his first endorsement deal with a Boston-based sportswear behemoth. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, New Balance released a commercial via Instagram officially unveiling St. John’s Prep junior Chris Vargas as a New Balance athlete. "Rooted in Boston. United by a love for the game," the company wrote in the caption. "We're proud to welcome local five-star quarterback prospect Chris Vargas to the New Balance family." Vargas, a Lawrence native who grew up a 10 minute drive from the company's factory in the city, said the feeling of earning an endorsement while still in high school was unbelieveable. "Just a small kid from Lawrence, Massachusetts, where Massachusetts isn't really like a big football state to play in... being a part of this New Balance family as a high school player is something that I'd never imagine would happen," Vargas said in the ad, which later shows him bringing New Balance cleats and signing autographs for Lawrence Pop Warner players, the place he says is "where it all began." The Ohio State commit , who highlights a crop of talented high school quarterbacks coming out of the Bay State , is having another monster season for the Eagles (11-0, 4-0 Catholic Conference), going 120-of-177 passing for 1,957 yards and 23 touchdowns while allowing just a pair of interceptions. On Oct. 30 in a Catholic Conference matchup with back-to-back MIAA Division 2 champions Catholic Memorial , Vargas went 12-of-21 passing for 203 yards and a pair of touchdowns to hand the Knights a 42-35 loss and secure the league title for the Danvers-based school. Vargas and the rest of the undefeated SJP squad have a pair of games remaining: first taking on arch-rivals Xaverian in their annual Thanksgiving showdown at home on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 7 p.m. before the top-seeded Eagles take on No. 2 St. John's Shrewsbury (10-1, 3-1 Catholic Conference) in the MIAA Division 1 Super Bowl at Boston College's Alumni Stadium on Saturday, Dec. 5, with an 11:30 a.m. kickoff scheduled. The Pioneers only loss of the year so far came against SJP on Oct. 16 , a 44-20 Eagles win in which Vargas tossed a pair of touchdown passes. item.title: Michigan's latest self-inflicted disaster proves yet again the Wolverines have a leadership problem
item.description: So let's make sure we have this straight. The University of Michigan, which has known since late July that outgoing athletic director Warde Manuel's last day would be Dec. 31, rushed to hire Trev Alberts as its new athletic director last week. The decision was made by incoming school president C. Cybele Raver, who hadn't even officially started yet but sped up the AD search so that Michigan could ostensibly fire football coach Kyle Whittingham and run a coaching search as quickly as possible. Then, upon agreeing to terms with Alberts, who resigned from his job at Texas A&M, Michigan learned through media reporting about Alberts' somewhat questionable comments from a deposition related to a human-resources issue two jobs ago at Nebraska. Because those comments were going to draw negative attention to Alberts, and Raver was going to have to answer some uncomfortable questions of her own to start her tenure, she decided to pull the plug on the whole deal and start over . A source with knowledge of the situation told Yahoo Sports that Raver made the decision to blow up the hire on her own over the objections of key regents, who had met over the weekend to discuss the deposition and approved the hire anyway. It's going to cost Michigan millions. It's going to have a major impact on urgent football decisions that probably shouldn't be made under these circumstances. It's going to make it exponentially harder for Michigan to hire a competent AD, which was already proving to be a challenge despite the amounts of money the school was throwing around. Other than that, great work Wolverines. Michigan won a football national title in 2023 and a men's basketball championship just seven months ago. Can you imagine what this school might be capable of with even somewhat competent leadership? Maybe one day, Michigan fans will be able to enjoy a stretch of years where they don't have to worry about a cheating scandal, criminal hackers as assistant coaches, recruiting violations or inappropriate relationships between coaches and employees. Unfortunately, that is not the era Michigan is in. Instead, it's an era of weak leadership, a politically motivated and meddlesome board of regents, and a university culture that doesn't seem to know what it wants to be. Trev Alberts previously worked as athletic director at Nebraska and Texas A&M. (Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) Steven Branscombe via Getty Images Now they've blown it up again — over, of all things, a guy trying to give a clinical answer in a deposition — and have become nothing less than the laughingstock of college sports. This is no way to run a big-time athletic department. And here's the worst part: Raver undoubtedly thinks she's doing the right thing. Though there's not a huge need to feel sorry for Alberts — one way or another, this career-altering misstep is going to result in millions of dollars hitting his bank account — this isn't the way to do business in college sports. item.title: 49ers fans took over Mexico City and turned it into a home game
item.description: Photo by Antonio Losada For the 2026 NFL season, the league decided to amplify its ever-expanding operation further, scheduling a record nine games outside the United States. As if the NFL needed any help growing its game, commissioner Roger Goodell got even luckier than he could have ever imagined and, for the international finale, set for Nov. 22 inside Estadio Banorte in Mexico City way before the season started, found himself stumbling into a premier matchup pitting the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers against a fellow contender from the NFC in the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings. Turns out, Mexico City wasn’t ready to allow any pesky Vikingo docking in the country to steal its Rojo y Oro . “I’m a fan since 1988. I was born in 1978. I’ve been following the team since I was 10, for nearly 40 years,” Alain Morales said. “I started watching Joe Montana sling the football even though my father rooted for San Francisco’s rivals. I wanted none of that.” Since I stepped into the biggest North American city for a third time in life, I could feel the 49ers Faithful presence everywhere. I had seen it from a distance before, but this time, I decided to start attending watch parties, talking to superfans from the official fan chapter , blending with them, and everything in between. They embraced and welcomed me from the get-go. I ended up participating in a Halloween costume party, cutting birthday cake gifted by someone I had never met, and eating pan de muerto with agua de jamaica . I first landed in Mexico City over a year ago, enthused and enticed from an ocean afar. Although my official 49ers rite of passage happened just a few moons ago at the start of my third time here, I had noticed something way before getting into the local Niners-catered scene rooted deep in Mexico’s soil. Step outside, and you’ll inevitably find tons of folks proudly wearing their Club América — the most-followed and winningest club in Liga MX, Mexico’s top-flight soccer league — jerseys. Look beyond, however, and you’ll notice big, oversized at times, red-and-white jerseys popping. No wonder San Francisco brought them. So for such a behemoth of an event as an NFL game in Mexico City, which last happened in 2022 and hadn’t happened since before COVID entered our lexicon, and featuring the team from The Bay, no less, you could rest assured the streets would be flooded with full-blown Niner aficionados , Mexican or not. “I’m originally from Miami, and I became a 49ers fan growing up watching Jerry Rice and watching them play, so I always cheer for them since I was six years old,” visiting Mike Brown said at the entrance to Estadio Banorte. “Now, I live in California, so I’m much more excited to be able to watch them every week. item.title: 2026 BMW Australian PGA field features several PGA Tour players, former LIV golfers
item.description: It's only been two weeks since Rory McIlroy clinched his fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title to cap off the DP World Tour's 2025-26 season, and now, a new season begins. The BMW Australian PGA Championship takes place this week at The Lakes Golf Club in Sydney, Australia, where David Puig is back to defend his title from a year ago, when he won by two shots as a member of the now-defunct LIV Golf league. Puig isn't the only former LIV golfer set to tee it up in Sydney this week, either. Aussie Cam Smith is trying to win the BMW Australian PGA for the fourth time in his career, while 2024 champion Elvis Smylie and 2016 winner Harold Varner III look to regain the title. Several other former members of the breakaway circuit, like Marc Leishman, Michael La Sasso, Tom McKibbin, Josele Ballester, Ben An, Caleb Surratt and Thomas Pieters, will also compete. The PGA Tour will be well-represented, too, with the likes of two-time BMW Australian PGA winner Adam Scott, 2023 champion Min Woo Lee and 2008 champion Geoff Ogilvy set to tee it up in front of a home crowd, along with other Tour members such as Corey Conners, Alex Noren and Sudarshan Yellamaraju. item.title: Tigers agree on one-year deal with veteran infielder Ha-Seong Kim
item.description: DETROIT — It’s unusual for Tigers’ president Scott Harris to tip his hand, even a little bit. But during a press conference Tuesday, Nov. 24, to announce a six-year, $46.5 million extension for pitcher Troy Melton , he dropped a hint. “We’ve made some moves that haven’t been announced yet,” he said. “We are going to continue to add arms but we also want to protect those arms and make sure we tighten up our infield defense. We want to make sure we can translate soft contact into outs more effectively that we have recently.” To that end, the Tigers have reached an agreement with veteran infielder Ha-Seong Kim on a one-year deal worth $5 million. The deal, which is pending medicals, was first reported by ESPN and confirmed to The Detroit News. Kim, 31, won a Gold Glove with the Padres in 2023, but he’s been injured the last two seasons, limited to 48 games with the Braves and Rays in 2025, and 51 games with the Braves last season. Still, although he only hit .161 in those 51 games, he was still a plus-4 defensive runs saved. He had shoulder surgery in 2025 and tore a tendon in his right middle finger last winter when he slipped on the ice back in South Korea. But the six-year veteran was healthy from the middle of July on last season, finishing the year with the Braves and playing in two playoff games. He can play shortstop, second base and third base and joins a mix that includes presumed regulars Kevin McGonigle (shortstop, third base), Javier Báez (shortstop, second base), Hao-Yu Lee (second base and third base) and Colt Keith (third base, first base), plus Tsung-Che Cheng (shortstop, second base), Max Anderson (second base) and John Peck (shortstop). item.title: Gabe Ouellette carries his family's Bristol football legacy into one last Battle for the Bell
item.description: Bristol Central senior Gabe Ouellette poses for a photo after a high school football practice on Nov. 19, 2026, in Bristol. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) BRISTOL - The name Ouellette has been synonymous with football in the Bell City since Gerry Ouellette played at Bristol Central in the mid-1980s. It's only fitting that the fifth and final member of the Ouellette family to play football in Bristol will suit up one last time on Thanksgiving morning in the annual Battle for the Bell. Gabe, the youngest of four brothers, is a senior quarterback for Bristol Central (4-5), which faces Bristol Eastern (1-8) at Muzzy Field at 10:30 a.m. "It feels crazy because I've grown up listening all about football," Gabe Ouellette said following practice on the Thursday before Thanksgiving. "My whole life has been football, to be able to watch great football players. There was a little bit of pressure, so I feel good that I was able to hold my own with them, but I'm happy about it. I'm happy about everything." The first Ouellette Gerard "Gerry" Ouellette, the father, ran for 1,335 yards in 1984, his senior season at Bristol Central. "You talk to some of the old-timers about their dad Gerry, it was the same thing (as the sons)," said current Central head coach Jeff Papazian, a quarterback for the Rams in the 1990s. "Not the biggest guy in the world, but played extremely hard and could run away from you and separate." Three Ouellettes, three Lancers Three of Gerry Ouellette's sons - Dylon, Tyler and Gerry III - played for Eastern. "The Ouellette brothers' time here at Bristol Eastern was defined by toughness. All three of them had that in common," said current Eastern head coach Anthony "AJ" Julius, who was an assistant coach when the brothers played for the Lancers. Dylon, 33, was the first Ouellette brother to play high school football in Bristol. In the 2010 Battle for the Bell, he ran for 208 yards on 18 carries and was named the team's offensive player of the game. That topped his father's mark of 189 yards on 18 carries in the 1984 game. Dylon also surpassed his father's season total with 1,391 yards in 2010. Eastern made the Class L state playoffs, losing at Masuk. Dylon graduated in 2011. Tyler, 31, also played for Eastern (Class of 2012), but his career was limited by two torn ACLs. "Tyler displayed great athletic ability but unfortunately was battling injuries a lot during his years here," Julius said. "He was a good teammate and hard worker. I have no doubt he would have been successful if not for injuries." Gabe agreed with Julius' assessment. "He probably would have been the best one, but he tore his ACL twice and gave it up," Ouellette said. "It was in the state championship game of an eighth-grade (Bristol) Bulldogs game, when he was carrying like three people. My dad said he tore his ACL." item.title: The Top 100 Cubs of all time, No. 87: Rogers Hornsby
item.description: Rogers Hornsby was one of the greatest MLB players ever. Of this, there is no doubt nor question. Rogers Hornsby was also one of the most disliked MLB players and managers ever — and there’s little doubt of that, too. Hornsby played 12 outstanding years for the Cardinals from 1915-26 and won the NL MVP award in 1925. He’d have won more of those if the award had existed prior to that, and the 1925 award was pre-BBWAA. He had five seasons of 10 or more bWAR in St. Louis and his 12.1 bWAR season in 1924, in which he batted .424/.507/.696, is one of the greatest MLB seasons ever. He was also the Cardinals’ manager in 1925 and 1926, and per his SABR biography he received “very high praise” for his managing abilities. Nevertheless, he wanted to renegotiate his contract, which had a year remaining, and Cardinals owner Sam Breadon got so frustrated with Hornsby that he traded him to the Giants. Hornsby lasted only one year there before being sent to the Braves and then, before the 1929 season, was traded to the Cubs for Bruce Cunningham, Percy Jones, Lou Legett, Freddie Maguire, Socks Seibold and $200,000. That was a tremendous sum of money in those days, roughly equivalent to $4 million today. The deal was made largely because the Braves were in financial trouble and needed the money badly. Hornsby immediately paid dividends on the field. You’ve probably heard a lot about his 1929 MVP season in comparison to Pete Crow-Armstrong’s great 2026 season, and in 1929 Hornsby batted .380/.459/.679 with 39 home runs, a league-leading 156 runs and 409 total bases, which to this day ranks fourth in Cubs history. That’s when things began to turn sour for Hornsby. He had a broken ankle in 1930 which limited him to just 42 games. The injury was one of the biggest reasons the Cubs didn’t repeat as NL champions in 1930, finishing just two games out of first place. And then Cubs owner William Wrigley made a decision that was franchise-altering. From the SABR bio: Cubs owner William Wrigley had become disenchanted with Joe McCarthy and announced with four games left in the season that Hornsby would take over as player-manager for 1931. Although there were rumors that Hornsby had undermined McCarthy and actively sought his job, the Rajah denied it, saying the two had parted as friends. Others, like teammates Gabby Hartnett and Charlie Grimm, were not convinced. Cubs president William Veeck, Sr. was so upset at Hornsby’s hiring that he resigned, only to come back when Wrigley promised he would never interfere again. Veeck put up with what has been characterized as Hornsby’s “reign of terror” for about a season and a half before firing him on August 2, 1932. In the interim Hornsby had gotten cross-ways with just about everyone on the team, including stars like Gabby Hartnett, Hack Wilson, Kiki Cuyler, and Billy Herman. item.title: Survey: Will the Giants put it all together against the Colts?
item.description: ﻿The New York Giants offense huddles before a play | Getty Images The New York Giants are riding high after — once again — coming up with a win as underdogs. Very few people thought the Giants would beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are widely considered among the best and most complete teams in the NFL. The most optimistic among us believed that there was a path for the Giants to come up with the win, but weren’t sure if they could execute. As it turned out, they did. They were able to do just enough on offense to establish a lead while their defense turned in a dominant performance for most of the game. It was a great game by the Giants, but it wasn’t a complete game. The offense was still inconsistent and plagued by turnovers, miscues, and penalties. And while the defense was able to pick them up, they were gassed by the end of the game because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive after Cam Skattebo’s fumble. The Giants’ win over the Jags is proving to be even bigger than anticipated, with the rest of the NFC East winning as well. That makes the upcoming game against the Indianapolis Colts into much more of a “must win” than it was before the Washington Commanders’ upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals. This is the time for the Giants to begin peaking if they want to be competitive in their upcoming games against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions. So this week we want to ask the Big Blue View community: Can the Giants put it all together and play a complete game against the Colts? Your choices this week are: A) Yes – The Giants’ offense and defense will play a complete 60 minute of football against the Colts. B) No – The mistakes and miscues will return, but there will be marked improvement over previous weeks. C) No – The offense is too mistake prone, with too many new players (J.J. item.description: Relief pitcher Brandyn Garcia (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Inspiration . The Diamondbacks bullpen was the best it’s been in years. But of the 29 Diamondbacks who pitched in relief, more than half are no longer on the Diamondbacks roster. Will acquisition of relief pitchers be impacted by the expectation that next season’s team salary will be less than this season? Data from Baseball Reference, Spotrac, and FanGraphs. Which relief pitchers will be back next season? Following are two tables: the first shows pitchers who are currently gone, and the second shows pitchers who are likely to return next season. Each table shows relief pitchers, their unadjusted cash salary for their relief appearances (rounded to the nearest $100,000), their age, their estimated bWAR earned in relief, were they with the Dbacks in 2025, and if they are gone, what happened. Note that the names of returning relievers are in purple text. There are 10 relief pitchers who remain on the roster (and one of the ten is catcher Adrian Del Castillo who may on rare occasion pitch in relief next season). They earned a total of $5.4 Million while earning 4.4 bWAR. In addition, their average age is 26.1 years old (Baseball Reference age for 2026 season). That compares well with the average of 31.0 years old for those taken off the roster. For two reasons (excellent performance by the retained relievers and the retained relievers were younger), the retained relief pitchers are a great core to build around for next season. However, the retained relief pitchers will not be enough. In total, they pitched 33% of the relief innings. Even if they increased their innings pitched by 50%, they will cover only half the needed innings. Additional relief pitchers will be needed. How much will Diamondbacks spend on relief pitchers? In 2023, when the Diamondbacks reached the playoffs, and again in 2026, the bullpen’s share of the total adjusted payroll was 12%. Perhaps 12% is the optimal bullpen spending to maximize team wins. item.description: Alex Pereira is a two-time light heavyweight champion | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC Daniel Cormier understands the conundrum Navajo Stirling and Carlos Ulberg are currently dealing with. Stirling scored an impressive knockout over Jiri Prochazka in this past Saturday’s UFC Qatar main event to remain undefeated and leave little doubt that he is a top contender at 205 pounds, arguably No. 1. However, Ulberg, the current champion of the division, just so happens to be Stirling’s friend and teammate, and the two have been reluctant to commit to a potential matchup. Matchmakers are unlikely to make a decision on the matter anytime soon, but the situation could become more urgent if two-time light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira returns to the division. Pereira vacated his title to commit to chasing gold at heavyweight, but if he loses to Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335, it could prompt a move back to the division he previously conquered, especially if an immediate title shot awaits. “If Alex Pereira loses, he goes down, I think he gets a title fight right away,” Cormier said on his YouTube channel. “Nobody goes before Pereira if it doesn’t work out at heavyweight. Pereira gets a title fight right away, but [Dominick] Reyes, [Paulo] Costa, both, [Magomed] Ankalaev, all three of those guys are very tough. “It feels like to me, lately, the wins from these guys, they don’t match up to what Navajo’s done, because Costa beat the kid that Reyes beat last, before, and again, they’re not former champions. I think Navajo Stirling’s the No. 1 contender right now.” Following his win, Stirling told reporters, “We’ll cross that bridge” when the time comes for there to be serious talks about him fighting Ulberg, who is currently on the shelf dealing with a knee injury suffered in his own win over Prochazka for the vacant belt this past April. Rymer predicted the Yankees would go big and add Brandon Lowe and Casey Schmitt. Lowe is a clear fit for the Yankees. item.title: 'I do feel pressure': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi opens up after record-breaking double century
item.description: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have rewritten the List A record books with a breathtaking 53-ball double century, but the teenager revealed that there was no change in his mindset going into the record-breaking innings against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 on Tuesday. The 15-year-old smashed an astonishing 204 off just 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes, the most ever by a batter in List A cricket, as India A chased down UAE's 250-run target in just 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets in their Group B encounter in Doha. Sooryavanshi registered the fastest century and double century in List A cricket, reaching the 100-run milestone in just 28 balls before completing his double hundred off 52 deliveries. He also became the first batter to score two List A half-centuries in 16 balls or fewer. Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Sooryavanshi explained that his approach was initially to spend time at the crease after failing to convert his starts in the previous two matches. However, he quickly realised that the surface offered little assistance to the bowlers and decided to back his natural attacking game. "In the last two matches, I got set but couldn't convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren't getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths," Sooryavanshi said. The left-hander revealed that his focus was simply on assessing the conditions and adjusting his approach accordingly, rather than thinking about records or milestones. "There wasn't anything specific on my mind. The only thought was that if the wicket was helping the bowlers, I would take my time and play a longer innings. But thankfully, that wasn't the case. The wicket was good, the ball was coming nicely onto the bat, so I tried to back my game," he added. 'Same mindset of trying to bat deep' Despite producing one of the most extraordinary innings in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi insisted that his mindset remained unchanged. He said his priority was always to bat deep and take control of the game once he settled in. "Nothing different, sir. It was the same mindset of trying to bat deep. If the game wasn't in my control initially, I would look to take my time. But thankfully, I was able to take control early on, and then I played the game on my terms," he said. Sooryavanshi also spoke about his experience of captaining Bihar, describing it as an enjoyable responsibility. item.title: Wirtz says he is in best form since £116m Liverpool move – and hails Iraola influence
item.description: Wirtz says he is in best form since £116m Liverpool move – and hails Iraola influence Florian Wirtz says he is in his best form since joining Liverpool and insists he never doubted his ability despite the criticism surrounding his debut season. The German international has looked transformed of late, registering three goals and six assists this season. Wirtz most recently scored and assisted in Sunday’s 4-0 win over Manchester United and believes his a greater understanding of English football have helped him rediscover his form. “I’d probably say I’ve been in the best form I have been in since I moved to Liverpool,” Wirtz said ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Club Brugge. “I can’t really say I’ve changed that much. I’ve become a bit better on a physical level and that’s the only reason I could explain it. “I also started to know English football and the league better. At the moment I’m feeling very good. I’m enjoying my football at Liverpool and I’m happy with how it’s going.” The 23-year-old joined Liverpool from Bayer Leverkusen for £116m in 2025 and endured a difficult first season, but insists individual statistics have never been his main focus. “My priority is that the club and the team are successful,” he said. “I know offensive players get judged by numbers and I’m always trying to use my opportunities when I have them. “But for me, it’s about the success of the team. I just want to play the best football I can play.” Wirtz also credited Andoni Iraola with helping restore his confidence. “I’m really enjoying playing under him,” he said. “He is bringing me back to a place where I was maybe two years ago, where I played really good football. “I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I’m really happy about that. I’m just trying to give him back what he gives me.”

item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Minnesota Timberwolves have received an encouraging update on Donte DiVincenzo, with the veteran guard targeting his season debut shortly before or after the New Year. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania , DiVincenzo has received full clearance for team activities and successfully completed five-on-five scrimmages in recent weeks. That puts the 29-year-old another step closer to rejoining a Minnesota team that has continued winning without him throughout the season’s opening month. The Timberwolves confirmed Tuesday that DiVincenzo is cleared for team basketball activities, although he remains out with no official return date. The Athletic’s Jon Krawczynski reported that DiVincenzo is aiming for January. His return to full practices will help determine when he can make the jump from rehabilitation to NBA competition. DiVincenzo ruptured his right Achilles during Game 4 of Minnesota’s first-round playoff series against the Denver Nuggets on April 25 and underwent surgery the following day. A return around New Year would come just over eight months after the operation. That would be a notably quick comeback . item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
